title: Control plane stakeholder Q&A & objection playbook for VPC/on-prem
purpose: Practical messaging and concise technical counters for sales and solutions teams when discussing Redwood's control plane options with regulated buyers. Focus on VPC and on-prem deployment requirements that typically come from CISO/Compliance/Platform engineering audiences.
one_liners: We separate control from compute: your model execution stays in your network; Redwood coordinates only metadata and optional telemetry under customer policy.
Deploy private control with no egress by default — telemetry is opt-in and can be routed over a customer-managed channel.
Our rollout model lets you start air-gapped in a staging VLAN and enable managed rollouts to production once compliance artifacts are accepted.
positioning_statements: For security teams: 'Minimal handshake, maximum auditability' — control-plane operations are cryptographically attested and stored in customer-controlled object stores when requested.
For platform teams: 'Declarative config, reproducible rollouts' — we support immutable artifacts, config-as-code for model pinning, and rollback-safe deployments.
For procurement: 'Predictable ops with exit options' — reserved capacity and private licensing with clear export and deprovisioning clauses to avoid vendor lock-in.
stakeholder_messages: CISO: We do not store inference inputs by default. When telemetry is required, we offer customer-side filtering and hashed pointers so raw data never leaves the VPC.
VP Engineering: The control plane only orchestrates; kernels, KV caches and model binaries remain on your compute nodes. Rolling upgrades are canary-first with automatic fallbacks.
Compliance Officer: We provide an exportable audit bundle (signed manifests + delivery receipts) that maps requests to policy decisions for SOC/ISO audits.
Procurement: Pricing for Private includes a platform license and an optional managed support tier; contracts include data handling SLAs and termination data-return clauses.
Solutions Engineer: Demo the 'no-telemetry' toggle and show a live canary rollback triggered by a simulated model regression.
buyer_objections: Objection: 'We can just self-host and avoid any external control plane.' Response: Self-hosting avoids external services but increases maintenance burden: patching, rollout automation, kernel tuning, and audit bundles. Redwood's private option gives the same network isolation while offloading upgrade orchestration, performance tuning and SLA-backed support so your team focuses on product features, not runtime plumbing.

Objection: 'We need zero data egress — how can any control plane still be safe?' Response: Our default architecture supports zero egress for inference traffic. Control-plane operations can be mediated via a customer-controlled side channel (VPN/PrivateLink) or run a local control component that only syncs signed manifests on an admin schedule. Telemetry is disabled until explicitly enabled with consent and filters.

Objection: 'Third-party control plane is a regulatory risk.' Response: We provide legal and technical mitigations: (1) option for on-prem control plane deployment, (2) customer-managed key material (KMS/HSM) for all secrets, (3) signed audit bundles exported on demand, and (4) contract terms for data locality and attestations.

Objection: 'We don't want vendor lock-in.' Response: Exportable manifests (model versions + config) and standardized deployment artifacts (OCI layers or tarballs) let you migrate to self-managed infra or another vendor with your model binaries intact. We provide a migration runbook as part of the enterprise package.

Objection: 'How do we prove uptime and performance for auditors?' Response: We offer SLA-backed observability reporting, time-series exports for latency/cost per-token, and third-party benchmarks that map our hardware profiles to real-world tail latencies.
competitive_notes: Cloud provider managed endpoints (GCP/Azure/AWS): Pros: integrated cloud services, single-bill. Cons: often black-box runtime, limited model lifecycle controls, and region-bound compliance gaps — harder to get declarative rollouts and signed audit bundles tailored to inference workloads.

Open-source self-hosted runtimes (external vendors): Pros: full control, often cheaper at massive scale. Cons: no SLA, heavier ops, missing performance tuning expertise (kernel choices, continuous batching), and limited enterprise-grade support for regulated audits.

Other LLM API providers: Pros: simplicity. Cons: telemetry and data-retention policies are often opaque and built for hosted use; few offer a private on-prem control plane with customer-managed keys and exportable audit evidence.

Redwood position: We combine enterprise-grade controls (KM integration, signed manifests, exportable audit bundles) with a performance-first runtime and a configurable control plane that can be hosted by customer or Redwood depending on compliance needs.
demo_talking_points: Show default 'no telemetry' deployment then enable filtered telemetry and demonstrate how the audit bundle is generated and signed.
Run a canary deployment and trigger an automatic rollback from the control plane UI; show the rollback policy config and associated signed manifest.
Walk through the key rotation flow using customer KMS and confirm that control-plane secrets are never readable by Redwood personnel.
Simulate a compliance request: export a time-bounded request log + signed evidence and show how it maps to policy decisions.
technical_handoff_notes: Config model: YAML manifests (model, route, rollout) stored in customer S3 or Git; control plane reads signed manifests only.
Telemetry modes: none / push-cut-through / push-filtered; all modes can be routed over customer VPC endpoints.
Fallbacks: local-serving agent can take over if control-plane heartbeat fails for X minutes; recommend SRE set X >= 5m for production.
KMS: support for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and external HSM via PKCS#11; keys are referenced by URI, not transmitted.
faq_snippets: Q: Will Redwood ever access plaintext inference data? A: Not unless you enable telemetry and explicitly permit plaintext collection. Default mode never transmits inference payloads.
Q: How are upgrades handled? A: Control-plane orchestrated upgrades are canary-first, with automated health checks and signed rollback manifests to ensure auditability.
Q: Can we run the control plane completely on-prem? A: Yes — we provide an on-prem control plane package for customers that need full air-gap or regulatory isolation.
next_steps: Action items for GTM: 1) Bake the 'no-telemetry' demo into the SE checklist; 2) Update the legal template with explicit audit-bundle SLA language; 3) Create a one-pager for procurement summarizing export and migration guarantees; 4) Run a dry-run with two pilot customers (finance and healthcare) and capture edge objections.
body: Working notes — do not publish: this doc is an opinionated cheat-sheet for SEs and AMs preparing for compliance-heavy buyer conversations. Keep examples concrete, link to the confluence design notes, and log any new objections back into JIRA-RDW-3342 so product can track common asks.
